formName: Intake - Combined Consent and Information Forms

fields.text:
This document contains several related forms that together allow Kinder Minds Limited to provide services to the Client and ensure you understand your rights, our processes, and how we manage information.

This document may be completed by:

  • the Client, where they are an adult or a young person able to give informed consent for themselves; or

  • a parent/legal guardian of the Client, where consent is being given on the Client’s behalf.


For the purposes of this document:
  • A young person aged 16 or over is presumed able to consent to their own healthcare under the Care of Children Act 2004, unless there are reasonable grounds to believe they lack capacity.
  • A young person under 16 years may consent for themselves only if they are assessed as having sufficient maturity and understanding to make the decision.

For clarity throughout this document:
  • “Client” refers to the person who will be seen by Kinder Minds for assessment and/or treatment.
  • “Parent/legal guardian” refers to those who hold legal guardianship for an under-18 Client.
  • “Primary Guardian” refers to the guardian who engages Kinder Minds for the Client or who is identified as the Primary Guardian in the patient registration form.
  • “Primary Contact” refers to the person Kinder Minds will communicate with for care-related matters:

    • this is the Client where they are aged 16 years or over, or where they are under 16 and assessed as able to consent for themselves; or

    • the Primary Guardian where a Client under 18 requires guardian consent.

  • “Kinder Minds Services” refers to mental health assessments, diagnostic formulation, therapeutic support, medication assessment and management, professional consultations, clinical correspondence, and follow-up care.
This combined document includes:
  • Identification and Authority – Establishes who the Client is and who has the legal authority to consent to Kinder Minds Services and complete this document.
  • General Information Consent – Confirms consent to receive Kinder Minds Services, outlines your rights, and explains how we manage and share health information.
  • Kinder Minds Terms of Service – Sets out the conditions under which Kinder Minds provides services, including fees, communication processes, cancellations, guardian responsibilities, and clinic policies.
  • Consent for Use of Automatic Scribe Technology – Describes information about our secure scribe tool and requests consent for its use.
  • Therapy Dog Request and Consent – Provides information about our therapy dog during in-person sessions and includes the required consent if you choose to opt in.
Please ensure all relevant sections are completed before signing the final declaration.

This section establishes who the Client is and who has the legal authority to provide consent for Kinder Minds Services. This ensures that all later consents, choices, and agreements in this document are valid and correctly attributed.

This form may only be completed by:

  • the Client, where they are able to give informed consent for themselves; or

  • a parent or legal guardian of the Client, where consent is being given on the Client’s behalf.


For Clients under 18 who are not able to consent independently, New Zealand law requires consent from all legal guardians before Kinder Minds can provide non-routine psychiatric services, unless the clinician assesses the young person as having capacity to consent.

Please tick the appropriate option regarding who is completing this form to give Kinder Minds consent to see the Client:

options.value: I am the Client named in Section 2.1 form and am giving consent for myself (please tick "Not applicable in Sections 2.3.1 & 2.3.3 and proceed to Section 3.1. If you are under 18, please also read Section 2.4.1 about communication with parents or guardians)
I am a parent/legal guardian of the above-named Client, and I am giving consent on their behalf (proceed to Section 2.3)

sections.label: 2.3.	Identifying Legal Guardians (Required Only for Clients Under 18)

fields.text:
This section applies where the Client is under 18 and does not have capacity to consent for themselves. In these cases, this section must be completed by a parent or legal guardian.

Kinder Minds provides Specialist Psychiatric Services. Under New Zealand law (Care of Children Act 2004), these services are considered non-routine medical treatment. This means that decisions about whether the Client receives these services must be made jointly by all legal guardians.
As a result:
  • All legal guardians must agree before Kinder Minds can provide services to the Client.
  • Consent is obtained by each legal guardian completing and returning a copy of this Combined Consent and Information document.
  • If a person’s guardianship has been removed by a Court order, they are not considered a legal guardian and do not need to provide consent.
All required copies of this Combined Consent and Information document must be completed and returned by the relevant legal guardians before appointments can be booked.

For the purposes of this form, a sole guardian means that you are the only person who currently holds legal guardianship of the Client under the Care of Children Act 2004.

You are a sole guardian only if:

  • no other person has ever held guardianship of the Client; or

  • any other person who previously held guardianship has had that guardianship removed by a Court order; or

  • the other guardian is deceased.

Being the primary caregiver, day-to-day carer, or the only involved parent does not by itself make someone a sole guardian.

fields.label: Please tick the option that applies:

options.value: I am the sole parent/legal guardian for the above-named Client.    I confirm that no other person holds guardianship under the Care of Children Act 2004.    (Proceed to Section 2.3.2 and skip Section 2.3.3)
I am NOT the sole parent/legal guardian for the above-named Client.    (Proceed to Section 2.3.2 and then Section 2.3.3)
Not applicable – I am the Client and am consenting for myself

fields.text: Kindly provide full names and contact details for each parent/legal guardian including yourself.

Kinder Minds provides Specialist Psychiatric Services. Under the Care of Children Act 2004, this type of healthcare is considered non-routine medical treatment and therefore an important matter affecting a child’s care and upbringing. For important matters, all legal guardians are expected to make decisions jointly, which means we must obtain consent from all guardians before appointments can proceed.

To support this, Kinder Minds must ensure that every legal guardian is fully informed about the services being requested. The Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers’ Rights requires us to support informed choice and consent, which includes giving all guardians equal access to the information they need to make that decision.

To meet these legal and ethical obligations, Kinder Minds must contact all parent(s)/legal guardian(s) listed in Section 2.3.2 to:
  • inform them of the services being requested for the Client, and
  • provide them with a copy of these Combined Consent and Information Forms to be completed so as to obtain their consent.

fields.label: Do you consent to Kinder Minds contacting the other listed parents/legal guardians in Section 2.3.2 for this purpose?

options.value: Not applicable – I am the Client and am consenting for myself

fields.text:
If you have selected “No”:
You will be responsible for informing the other parent(s)/legal guardian(s) and ensuring they receive and complete this consent form. Kinder Minds cannot proceed with appointments until all required consents are obtained, unless the clinician determines that the young person is able to consent independently.
This section explains how Kinder Minds communicates with Clients and parents/legal guardians during care, depending on who is able to provide consent.

Where a Client under 18 (including a young person aged 16 or over) is able to give informed consent for themselves, the Client is treated as the primary decision-maker and primary contact for their care.

In this situation, Kinder Minds will communicate directly with the Client. Parents or legal guardians will only be included in communication where the Client has given consent, or where disclosure is required by law or necessary for safety.
fields.label: 2.4.1. Young People Consenting for Themselves

fields.text:
For Clients under 18 who are not able to consent for themselves, Kinder Minds involves all legal guardians in important healthcare decisions, including decisions about commencing assessment or treatment and significant changes to care.

Once care has commenced, routine communication (such as appointment confirmations, scheduling, rescheduling, follow-up administration, and report logistics) is managed through the Primary Guardian, being the guardian who engages Kinder Minds or who is identified as the Primary Guardian in the patient registration form.

This approach supports clear and efficient communication and does not limit the legal rights of any guardian. All legal guardians retain the right to request access to information about the Client’s care at any time, unless restricted by law or safety considerations.

Continue onto Section 3.
fields.label: 2.4.2. Clients Under 18 Who Require Guardian Consent

fields.text:
This section explains what Kinder Minds Services involve, your rights under New Zealand law, and how we manage and share health information.

By completing it, you are giving consent for Kinder Minds to provide services to the Client named in this document.

If the Client is under 18 and cannot consent for themselves, all legal guardians must provide consent, as outlined in Section 2.

Kinder Minds offers the following standard services (prices as of Jan 2026):
  • Neurodevelopment Assessment ($650 inc GST).
  • ADHD Assessment – Under 18 ($1,200 inc GST), Adult ($1,400 inc GST).
  • Autism Assessment ($2,500 inc GST).
  • Combined ADHD and Autism Assessment – Under 18 ($2,800 inc GST), Adult ($3,000 inc GST).
  • Medication Commencement/Review (for Clients we have diagnosed only) ($800 inc GST).
  • Post Diagnostic Support ($200/hr inc GST with our Specialist Nurse).
Our standard rate for clinician time is $500/hr (incl. GST).

These prices are subject to update, and the correct pricing will always be confirmed by email before appointments are booked.

The services offered by Kinder Minds may include, but are not limited to, clinical interviews; psychological and psychiatric assessment; diagnostic formulation; therapeutic support; medication assessment and management; written reports; communication and correspondence with GPs, schools, and other health providers; provision of medical certificates; and prescribing where clinically appropriate.

Before delivering any service, or any component of a service, Kinder Minds will ensure that the Client (or their parent(s)/legal guardian(s), where applicable) is fully informed about what the service or component involves. You will have the opportunity to ask questions and provide informed consent before clinical activities are undertaken.

Continue onto Section 3.2
fields.label: 3.1.	Kinder Minds Services

fields.text:
The Client has important rights under New Zealand law when receiving health services. These rights are protected by:
  • The Health and Disability Commissioner Act 1994 (HDC Act) and the Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers’ Rights (HDC Code)
    These set out your rights when receiving healthcare, including the right to be treated with respect, to be fully informed, to make choices about your care, and to give or refuse consent.
  • The Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992 (rare situations only)
    This Act outlines the limited circumstances where treatment may occur without consent if there is serious and imminent risk to the Client or others.
  • The Care of Children Act 2004 (CoCA)
    For Clients under 18, this Act sets out the rights of parents and legal guardians to participate in and make decisions about significant healthcare matters.
  • The Privacy Act 2020 and Health Information Privacy Code 2020 (HIPC)
    These laws protect your rights over your health information, including how it is collected, used, stored, shared, and accessed.
You can read more about these rights at:
  • Health and Disability Commissioner Act 1994 (HDC Act): https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/1994/0088/latest/whole.html#DLM333932
  • Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers’ Rights (HDC Code): https://www.hdc.org.nz/your-rights/about-the-code/code-of-health-and-disability-services-consumers-rights/
  • Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/1992/0046/latest/whole.html#DLM262180
  • Care of Children Act 2004 (CoCA): https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2004/0090/latest/whole.html
  • Privacy Act 2020: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2020/0031/latest/LMS23223.html
  • Health Information Privacy Code 2020 (HIPC): https://www.privacy.org.nz/privacy-principles/codes-of-practice/hipc2020/
fields.label: 3.2.	Your Rights When Receiving Care

fields.text:
You have the right to:
  • be fully informed about any assessment, treatment, or intervention
  • ask questions at any time
  • give, withhold, or withdraw consent
  • receive information in a way you can understand
fields.label: 3.2.1.	Your Rights to Information and Consent

fields.text:
When working with children and adolescents, Kinder Minds involves parents or legal guardians as required by law and, where appropriate, whānau.

If a young person is assessed as having sufficient age and competence and requests limits on parental involvement, this will be considered in accordance with New Zealand law and clinical judgement.
fields.label: 3.2.2.	Involvement of Parents, Guardians, and Whānau (for Clients Under 18)

fields.text:
Kinder Minds will only share information when consent has been given by the Client or their parent(s)/legal guardian(s), where applicable.

If you have any concerns about proposed information sharing, please discuss these with your clinician. You may change or withdraw consent at any time.

Details about how and with whom information may be shared are set out in Section 3.3.
fields.label: 3.2.3.	When Information Is Shared With Your Consent

fields.text:
In rare situations, Kinder Minds may need to share information without consent in order to protect the safety or wellbeing of the Client or others. This may occur if:
  • there is a serious and immediate risk of harm to the Client or another person; or
  • we are legally required to act under New Zealand law, including the Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992; or
  • there are concerns about a child’s safety that require involvement of child protection services, such as Oranga Tamariki.
These situations are uncommon. Wherever possible, Kinder Minds will discuss this with the Client and/or their parent(s)/legal guardian(s) before or as soon as practicable after information is shared.
fields.label: 3.2.4.	Rare Situations Where Information May Be Shared Without Consent

fields.text:
Kinder Minds protects your health information in accordance with the Privacy Act 2020 and the Health Information Privacy Code 2020 (HIPC).

Full details about how we collect, store, use, and protect your information are provided in Section 3.3.
fields.label: 3.2.5.	Privacy and Health Information

fields.text:
Kinder Minds protects your privacy and manages your information in accordance with the Privacy Act 2020 and the Health Information Privacy Code 2020 (HIPC).

This section explains how we collect, use, store, and share your information.
fields.label: 3.3.	Privacy and Data Use

fields.text:
We collect information necessary to provide safe and effective care. This may include:
  • personal and contact details
  • demographic information
  • clinical history and assessment information
  • educational or occupational information (where relevant)
  • information shared by your school, GP, or other professionals (with consent)
  • administrative information such as bookings, invoices, and communication records
  • audio recordings only when you have provided explicit consent (see Section 4)
fields.label: 3.3.1.	What Information We Collect

fields.text:
We use your information to:
  • provide assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up care
  • prepare clinical reports and communicate results
  • coordinate care with other health providers, schools, or support services (with consent)
  • ensure safe prescribing and clinical decision-making
  • manage bookings, communication, invoicing, and administrative processes
  • respond to safety concerns where required
We do not use your information for any purpose unrelated to your care unless legally required or you have given explicit consent. Where information is used for any purpose outside direct clinical care, Kinder Minds will take all reasonable steps to anonymise or de-identify it whenever possible.
fields.label: 3.3.2.	How We Use Your Information

fields.text:
Kinder Minds uses secure digital systems to manage your information:
  • Zanda Health (NZ-based): collects forms, consents, client details, and manages parts of the booking and invoicing workflow.
  • SharePoint (Microsoft 365): stores clinical documents, reports, and—if you have consented to recording—any related audio files.
  • Notion: stores organisational information relating to Clients, parent(s)/legal guardian(s), GPs, pharmacies, and other involved parties to support administration and coordination of care.
  • Xero: stores invoicing and payment information.
Only authorised staff involved in your care or administration have access to these systems.

All systems used by Kinder Minds are accessed through secure, password-protected accounts within networks under Kinder Minds’ administrative control. Access to these systems is restricted to authorised staff and protected by industry-standard security measures.
fields.label: 3.3.3.	Where and How Your Information Is Stored

fields.text:
Kinder Minds may use audio recording during appointments to support accurate clinical documentation.

Recordings are only made when you have provided explicit consent, which is obtained separately in Section 4 which explains how recordings are collected, used, stored, and deleted.
fields.label: 3.3.4.	Audio Recording and Documentation Tools

fields.text:
Kinder Minds shares health information only with your consent, unless a rare safety or legal exception applies (see Section 3.2.4).

With consent, information may be shared where clinically appropriate with:
  • parent(s) or legal guardian(s), where the Client is under 18 or where the Client has requested their involvement
  • the Client’s GP or other health professionals involved in their care
  • schools, educators, or education services where relevant to assessment or treatment
  • counsellors, therapists, or other support services involved in the Client’s care
  • any other support people or organisations nominated by the Client (or parent/legal guardian)
For Clients under 18, Kinder Minds involves all legal guardians as required by law and where reasonably practicable.

For Clients who can consent for themselves (young people or adults), information is shared only with the people or services they nominate.

You may change or withdraw consent for information sharing at any time.
fields.label: 3.3.5.	How Information Is Shared

fields.text:
Under the Privacy Act 2020 and HIPC, you have the right to:
  • access your health information
  • request correction of any information you believe is inaccurate
  • request deletion of information (subject to clinical and legal retention requirements)
  • ask how your information has been used or shared
You can make a request at any time by contacting Kinder Minds.
fields.label: 3.3.6.	Your Rights Over Your Information

fields.text:
If you have concerns about how your information is handled, please contact Kinder Minds directly.

You also have the right to complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner: https://www.privacy.org.nz

Continue onto Section 4
fields.label: 3.3.7.	How to Raise a Privacy Concern

fields.text:
These Terms of Service (“Terms”) apply to all services provided by Kinder Minds Limited (“we”, “our”, “us”). By engaging our services, you (“the Client”, or “parent/legal guardian” where applicable) agree to these Terms.

For under-18 Clients, the Primary Guardian is the guardian who engages Kinder Minds for services or who is identified as the Primary Guardian in the patient registration form. The Primary Guardian is responsible for administrative matters, including receiving invoices and settling accounts, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Our services are delivered in accordance with New Zealand law, including (as applicable):
  • the Health and Disability Commissioner Act 1994 and the Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers’ Rights
  • the Care of Children Act 2004
  • the Privacy Act 2020
  • the Health Information Privacy Code 2020
  • all relevant professional and clinical standards
fields.label: 4.1.	Introduction

fields.text:
Kinder Minds provides specialist psychiatric services, also covered in Section 3.1, including:
  • clinical interviews
  • psychiatric and neurodevelopmental assessments
  • diagnostic formulation
  • therapeutic support
  • medication assessment and management
  • follow-up consultations
  • clinical correspondence, reports, certificates, and referrals
Services may be delivered:
  • In person – at Kinder Minds’ consulting rooms; or
  • By telehealth – via secure videoconference (Zanda with Zoom or equivalent platform). You will need a stable internet connection, camera, and microphone.
fields.label: 4.2.	Scope of Services

fields.text:
• A clinical summary and/or report may be produced after sessions as part of your care.
  • We may correspond with and share relevant clinical information with your GP or other health providers unless you choose to opt out. Information may also be shared without consent only when required for safety or as permitted under New Zealand law.
fields.label: 4.2.1.	Session Summaries and Reports

fields.text:
Booking via client portal:
  • Clients are set up on our client portal to be able to make bookings for first appointments and follow-ups.
Bookings via phone/email:
  • At times, appointment options may be discussed or offered by phone or email.
  • Any appointment arranged this way will always be confirmed by email.
Reminders:
  • Where we have up-to-date contact details for the Client or primary parent/legal guardian, we will do our best to send courtesy reminders (typically one week and 48 hours before your appointment) via email and/or SMS.
  • If your phone number or email address changes, please inform us promptly.
  • These reminders are not guaranteed; you remain responsible for attending or cancelling on time (see Section 5.6.3).
Appointment details
  • Confirmation emails and/or reminder messages will include the appointment location and any required telehealth links.
fields.label: 5.3.	Appointment Booking and Communication

fields.text:
We are committed to protecting your privacy and confidentiality.
  • We comply with the Privacy Act 2020 and Health Information Privacy Code 2020 (HIPC).
  • Your information is stored securely using systems such as Zanda Health (forms, bookings, invoicing), Microsoft 365 (SharePoint/OneDrive for clinical documents), Xero (invoicing and reconciliation), and Notion (relationship mapping and contact context), with access restricted to authorised staff.
  • Use of automatic scribe technology (“Heidi”) only occurs if you have given separate consent (see AI Scribe Consent). Recordings used for Heidi are stored securely and deleted in line with our retention policies.
Full details of how we collect, store, use, and protect information are set out in Section 3.3 of this document.

You have the right to access and request correction of your information at any time. In the unlikely event of a notifiable data breach, we will inform you and take appropriate remedial action.
fields.label: 4.4.	Privacy and Confidentiality

fields.text:
Kinder Minds is not an emergency service.
  • If you are in immediate danger or crisis, call 111 or attend the nearest emergency department.
  • Our services are not a substitute for acute crisis care or 24/7 support.
Telehealth and technical issues:
  • If technical problems on your side (e.g. poor internet, device failure) prevent a session from proceeding or being completed, we may need to stop the session and arrange another time. Standard cancellation terms may still apply (see Section 5.6.3).
  • If technical issues are on our side, we will offer an alternative appointment time without additional clinical charge for the lost time.
Sessions are for the Client’s clinical needs. They are not a forum for resolving legal, separation, or custody disputes between parents or other parties.
fields.label: 4.5.	Limitations of Service

fields.text: This section forms the commercial/contractual basis of service.
fields.label: 4.6.	Terms of Trade (Fees, Payment, Cancellations, Liability)

fields.text:
• Current fees for our standard services are displayed on our website. The most up-to-date pricing will always be confirmed in writing—typically by email—before any appointment or service is booked.
  • Some services are offered at fixed rates, often with optional modular components that may be added depending on the individual needs of the Client’s care.
  • Additional or extended appointments—including separate parent-only consultations for under-18 Clients (see Section 5.7.3)—are billed at the standard clinician hourly rate and are not part of the fixed rate costs of the services offered.
  • Other services are billed based on the standard clinician hourly rate in effect at the time of booking.
  • Some tasks or documents are not listed on our website (for example, additional letters, medical certificates, extended reports, or follow-up documentation). These will always be discussed with you first, with clear confirmation of any costs, before we proceed.
fields.label: 4.6.1.	Fees

fields.text:
• We currently accept payment by bank transfer only.
  • Payment is due upon completion of the relevant service, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
    • A service may consist of one or more appointments and may include clinical work completed before, during, or after an appointment (for example, assessment preparation, information review, report writing, or clinical correspondence).
  • For Clients under 18, the Primary Guardian (as defined in Section 1) is responsible for payment to Kinder Minds. Any private cost-sharing arrangements between guardians are outside Kinder Minds’ involvement and must be resolved directly between the guardians.
  • If a service is cancelled or discontinued after Kinder Minds has already completed preparatory or pre-appointment work, we reserve the right to charge for the work already undertaken. Where such charges apply:
    • they will relate only to work already completed; and
    • you will be informed of the applicable charges at the time of cancellation or as soon as reasonably practicable.
    • No further work will be undertaken without your agreement.
fields.label: 4.6.2.	Payment

fields.text:
Because your appointment time is reserved specifically for you:
  • For standard appointments, we require at least three (3) working days’ notice (Mon–Fri, excluding public holidays) to cancel or reschedule without charge.
  • Cancellations with less notice than required, or failure to attend (“no-show”), will be charged at the full appointment fee.
As outlined in Section 5.3, Kinder Minds will attempt to provide courtesy reminders, but whether or not a reminder is received, you remain responsible for:
  • remembering your appointment time
  • notifying us in time if you cannot attend.
fields.label: 4.6.3.	Cancellation Policy

fields.text:
Where cancellation notice is given within the required timeframe:
  • We will offer the next available appointment time.
  • Due to high demand, re-booking may be several weeks away, and we cannot guarantee an earlier slot.
fields.label: 4.6.4.	Rescheduling

fields.text:
• Prescriptions are issued at the clinician’s professional discretion, based on clinical assessment and safety considerations.
  • Prescriptions are sent electronically to your nominated pharmacy where possible.
  • Ongoing prescribing may be contingent on recommended follow-up, monitoring, and/or shared-care arrangements with your GP.
fields.label: 4.6.5.	Prescription Services

fields.text:
• We are affiliated with ACC for specific services under the relevant ACC contracts (e.g. CPSA). Eligibility and referral pathways must be confirmed by ACC/Recovery Partners.
  • For other external funders (e.g. NGOs, agencies, or employers), funding arrangements must be confirmed in writing in advance. Where funding is not approved or lapses, responsibility for payment remains with the Client/guardian.
fields.label: 4.6.6.	ACC and Other Funders

fields.text:
• We are currently providers with Southern Cross and can process claims on your behalf once consent has been given for us to do so.
  • We may be recognised by other health insurance providers. Where applicable our admin team will assist with pre-approval by providing quotes.
  • For other insurers, seeking pre-approval and confirming eligibility is the Client’s responsibility.
  • We do not determine whether your insurer will reimburse any part of your fees. Any dispute about reimbursement is between you and your insurer and does not affect your obligation to pay Kinder Minds’ invoices.
fields.label: 4.6.7.	Health Insurance Providers

fields.text:
We are required to keep your health records for a minimum of 10 years from your last contact with us. We follow the Health (Retention of Health Information) Regulations 1996, as well as the Privacy Act 2020 and the Health Information Privacy Code 2020.

This may not apply if your full clinical file has been transferred to another provider or provided to you/your authorised representative in full.
fields.label: 4.6.8.	Records Retention

fields.text:
We will provide services with reasonable care and skill. However:
  • We do not guarantee any specific clinical outcome or improvement.
  • We are not liable for losses arising from:
    • failure or limitations of telehealth technology outside our control
    • delays or decisions made by third parties (e.g. schools, other providers, insurers, ACC)
    • incomplete or inaccurate information provided to us
    • unmet expectations regarding assessment outcomes, reports, or treatment responses.
fields.label: 4.6.9.	Liability

fields.text:
If you are having difficulty paying an invoice, please contact us as early as possible to discuss options.

Where payment disputes or ongoing unpaid balances significantly impact the clinical or administrative relationship:
  • non-urgent services may be paused; and/or
  • administrative fees may be applied after fair warning; and/or
  • we may consider discharging you from Kinder Minds and recommending alternative services.
This does not limit your right to seek urgent or emergency care through other providers.
fields.label: 4.6.10.	Payment Difficulties and Disputes

fields.text: (Applies only if the young person is not Gillick competent.)
fields.label: 4.7.	Additional Terms for Clients Under 18 (Joint Guardianship Requirements)

fields.text:
Under the Care of Children Act 2004 (CoCA):
  • Psychiatric assessment and treatment are generally considered non-routine medical treatment.
  • Legal guardians must, as far as practicable, act jointly and consult with each other about important decisions affecting the child’s care.
Therefore:
  • For Kinder Minds to offer services to Clients under 18, all legal guardians are expected to provide informed consent before assessment or treatment proceeds, unless the young person is assessed as having capacity to consent independently.
  • Guardians must disclose any court orders, parenting agreements, Protection Orders, or safety concerns that affect guardianship, consent, or communication.
  • If consent from all guardians has not been received before a scheduled appointment, Kinder Minds may need to cancel or postpone the booking in accordance with our cancellation policy (see Section 5.6.3).
  • These requirements apply to all referrals and bookings and form part of Kinder Minds’ intake and consent processes.
These requirements are reflected in the General Information and Consent sections of this form and in our intake processes.
fields.label: 4.7.1.	Legal Basis and Consent Requirements

fields.text:
• Both guardians have equal rights to health information unless restricted by court order or safety concerns.
  • Administrative communication may occur with the primary booking guardian, but this does not override legal rights.
fields.label: 4.7.2.	Communication With Guardians

fields.text:
• Both guardians are welcome to attend appointments.
  • Separate parent appointments (if requested) are optional, subject to availability, and billed separately.
fields.label: 4.7.3.	Appointment Attendance

fields.text:
Kinder Minds provides psychiatric services with the young person’s wellbeing as the primary focus. The child’s best interests remain our first and paramount consideration at all times, consistent with our clinical values and with New Zealand law.

If parental conflict interferes with the child’s consultations:
  • clinicians may redirect the session,
  • end the appointment early, or
  • require an additional (paid) session.
fields.label: 4.7.4.	Appointment Focus and Clinician Discretion

fields.text:
• Any guardian may request cancellation or rescheduling of a child’s appointment.
  • The guardian initiating the cancellation must promptly notify the other guardian(s) and make a genuine effort to consult and reach agreement on the decision.
  • Standard cancellation rules (see Section 5.6.3) apply, including fees for insufficient notice.
fields.label: 4.7.5.	Cancellation Authority for Child Appointments

fields.text:
• The Primary Guardian—being the parent/legal guardian who engages Kinder Minds or who is identified as the Primary Guardian in the patient registration form—is financially responsible for all invoices issued by Kinder Minds.
    • This includes fees for standard appointments and any additional services provided as part of the Client’s care, including separate or additional appointments requested by either guardian.
  • Any cost-sharing or reimbursement arrangements between guardians are private matters and are not managed, mediated, or enforced by Kinder Minds.
fields.label: 4.7.6.	Billing Responsibility

sections.label: 5.	Consent for Use of Automatic Scribe Technology

fields.text: Kinder Minds uses an automatic scribe technology (Heidi) to support accurate documentation of consultations and reduce administrative time, allowing clinicians to focus more fully on your care.

• Heidi is an AI-supported transcription tool used to assist in creating clinical notes and medical reports.
  • It transcribes the consultation audio into text, which clinicians use to draft reports, letters, and summaries.
  • Heidi does not make clinical decisions.
fields.label: 5.1.	What Heidi Does

fields.text:
If you consent to the use of Heidi:
  • All appointments from the point consent is given will be audio-recorded so that Heidi can generate an accurate transcript.
  • Recordings are stored securely in Kinder Minds’ Microsoft SharePoint, which is password-protected and accessible only to authorised clinical staff.
  • Recordings are retained for up to 6 months after Kinder Minds has completed care for the Client and all associated documentation has been finalised, after which the recordings are permanently deleted.
  • If Kinder Minds ever requires longer retention of recordings, we will request your explicit consent.
  • The use, storage, and deletion of recordings is further governed by our Privacy and Data Use policy (see Section 3.3).
fields.label: 5.2.	Recording and Storage

fields.text:
• All recordings, transcripts, and documents created through Heidi are managed in accordance with the Privacy Act 2020 and the Health Information Privacy Code 2020 (HIPC).
  • Information is not used for any purpose unrelated to your care unless required by law or with your explicit consent.
fields.label: 5.3.	Privacy and Security

fields.text:
You have the right to:
  • decline the use of Heidi
  • withdraw consent at any time (this will apply to future appointments)
  • request access to or deletion of recordings relating to your care, subject to legal and clinical safety requirements
  • ask questions before giving consent
If you choose not to consent, your clinician will complete notes manually. This may increase the time required for documentation and may affect the speed at which reports can be produced, but your access to care will not be affected.
fields.label: 5.4.	Your Rights

Neve is Kinder Minds’ therapy dog — a tender, gentle golden retriever who has been trained for safe interactions with both children and adults. She has experience working with many Clients and often helps people feel calmer and more comfortable during in-person sessions.
fields.label: 6.1.	About Neve: Kinder Minds’ Therapy Dog

fields.text:
Neve’s participation is entirely optional, and choosing not to have her present will not affect the care you receive.
Her attendance as a supporting companion depends on:
  • her availability on the day, and
  • logistical considerations for all Clients attending the clinic.
Kinder Minds will make every reasonable effort to accommodate your request; however, Neve’s presence is ultimately subject to the clinician’s judgement and discretion to ensure appropriate care on the day.
To request Neve’s attendance, the Therapy Dog Interaction Waiver (Sections 6.3 through 6.5) must be completed by either:

  • all parents/legal guardians (for Clients under 18).
